title: Earn-and-burn onboarding credit bursts + inertia-based upgrade hints
creator: Ariel Chen
description: Problem: Free-tier credits and trials at Redwood convert some users to paid plans but we see lower-than-expected early-week activation and high inertia mid-trial. Hypothesis: Delivering a short, upfront 'earn-and-burn' credit burst (larger ephemeral credit amount that expires quickly) will accelerate discovery of value and increase trial-to-paid conversion if paired with contextual, inertia-based upgrade hints timed to usage lulls. This ticket scopes an A/B/C experiment to test credit sizing, fast-expiry windows, and in-product upgrade hint triggers. The work requires billing / metering hooks, Console UX for hint surfaces, lightweight backend gating, and a security questionnaire update for enterprise contract language around credit refunds and auditability.
hypothesis: If new signups receive a short-lived, higher-value credit burst (3x base free credits) that expires in 7 days and see contextual upgrade hints when usage drops 2+ days in a row, then 14-day trial conversion to any paid tier will increase by >= 12% vs baseline without increasing support tickets by >20%.
experiment_design: Cohorts: Control (baseline 100 free credits, 30d expiry), Variant A (burst: 300 credits, 7d expiry, passive banner), Variant B (burst: 300 credits, 7d expiry, contextual upgrade hint after 48h inactivity), Variant C (moderate burst: 200 credits, 10d expiry, contextual hint). Randomize at signup. Exclude enterprise SSO accounts and existing customers. Track downstream attribution for conversions tied to credit exhaustion events. Rollout: 5% -> 20% -> 50% funnels over 2 weeks after QA. Metrics instrumentation: backend meter events for credit grants and consumption, evaluate per-cohort telemetry in console and Mixpanel.
measurement_plan: Primary metric: trial -> paid conversion within 14 days of signup. Secondary: time-to-first-paid-call, % users who exhaust burst credits, average session length, retention Day 7/14, support tickets flagged as billing/questions. Guardrail: Customer-reported confusion measured via in-app NPS prompt and support tag 'credits-confusion' must remain < 5% of new signups. Statistical plan: power to detect 12% relative uplift with alpha=0.05, estimate 6k signups across cohorts. Use Wilson CI and bucketed time-to-event analysis.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Instrumentation emits credit_grant and credit_consumption events for 100% of cohort signups. 2) UX surfaces for contextual hint show with correct frequency and are dismissible; experiment can be toggled remotely. 3) No P0 production incidents during 5% ramp. 4) Analysis notebook with cohort results published to shared Confluence page and benchmark vs baseline. 5) Security & legal sign-off on credit accounting language for enterprise contracts and audit logs.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature flags and backend proto in staging (ENG-60992). Phase 1: 5% production ramp for variant A/B/C; monitor telemetry and support for 48h. Phase 2: 20% ramp if no guardrail breaches; extended 2 weeks for signal. Phase 3: 50% ramp and final analysis window 14 days. Revert: remote kill-switch to remove burst grants and hint rules; support playbook ready. Release owner: Marcus Patel. Engineering lead: Priya Narang. Design lead: Sofia Rivera.
